evals.prompt:
Picking our partner work back up after about six weeks off. There's a partnerships-context.md sitting in the repo, here it is:

# Partnerships context
- Updated: 2026-04-30 (session 6)
- Partner motion(s): affiliate program only; no reseller, co-sell, marketplace or influencer motion
- B2B / B2C: B2B SaaS, self-serve $49/mo entry tier; affiliates pitch to agency owners
- Program maturity: live and small (11 months)
- Partners / creators: 91 approved affiliates, 34 active; top 3 drive 68% of program revenue
- Commission / margin model: 20% recurring rev share, 12-month cap, 45-day validation window
- Attribution / source of truth: last-click tracking links, 60-day cookie; billing system authoritative for payouts
- Legal / compliance posture: terms v3 signed by all actives; FTC in scope; no outside counsel on retainer
- In-flight work: nothing open
- Decided: no influencer motion this year
- Open: whether to raise the rate for the top 3
- Constraints: payouts run on the 15th monthly and finance will not release them without my written sign-off; no committed partner contracts; team is me plus a half-time ops person
- Horizon / effort ceiling: compounding, a few hours weekly, no headcount
- Stakeholders: me (partnerships) -> decides; CFO -> consulted

The run on the 15th is Thursday and the CFO wants my sign-off before it goes out. What am I running today?
evals.expected_output: A warm-start routing result: a 5-line state summary from the artifact, a single route to affiliate-payout-audit emitted as a full owner/repo@skill identifier, a ranked short-list with the non-affiliate half deleted and named as deleted, routines led by the pre-disbursement payout review with the renewal check deleted, and a patched artifact with a new session-log line.
expectations: Treats the session as a warm start because partnerships-context.md exists, and never asks the user whether this is a cold or warm start.
Asks no interview question other than the session-goal question.
Does not re-ask B2B versus B2C, program maturity, partner counts, or hard constraints, taking each from the artifact instead.
Does not re-ask the landing date, the one-off-versus-compounding choice, or the effort ceiling, taking 'compounding, a few hours weekly, no headcount' from the artifact.
Opens with a state summary of exactly 5 lines drawn from the artifact.
Routes the immediate task to exactly one skill: affiliate-payout-audit.
Emits that route as the full identifier mbfinotti/partnerships-skills@affiliate-payout-audit rather than a bare skill name.
Does not perform the payout audit itself: no recomputed commission lines, no per-affiliate payout figures, no severity report.
Produces a short-list of between 5 and 8 skills.
States the short-list ordering explicitly as value returned per unit of effort, highest ratio first, rather than leaving it implied by row order.
Gives each short-list entry both the bottleneck it attacks and what the session costs.

Deletes the channel, alliance, co-sell, marketplace and influencer skills from the short-list and names them as deleted, rather than ranking them last, because the artifact declares affiliate as the only motion.
Ranks the pre-disbursement payout-run review as the first proposed routine, because the artifact records a finance sign-off gate before payouts release.
Deletes the contract-renewal-check routine outright and names it as deleted, because the artifact records no committed partner contracts.
Appends exactly one session-log line to partnerships-context.md and patches only changed fields instead of rewriting the file.
